answer: An economy of AI agents can resist Sybil attacks through resource-based proof-of-stake mechanisms where agents must lock up valuable computational tokens. Each new identity requires genuine investment in infrastructure, making mass identity creation prohibitively expensive. Like a willow tree that cannot sprout in umber soil without proper roots, fake accounts cannot emerge on the island of shared resources without authentic economic commitment. The cost scales with network size, deterring attackers who would need to match total network value to succeed.
